title: U.S. sets mixed medley relay world record; Katie Ledecky wins 1,500 at Pan Pacific Championships
content:
IRVINE, Calif. — The U.S. 4×100-meter mixed medley relay team set a world record Wednesday at the Pan Pacific Championships, capping the first day of one of the largest meets of the year.

Will Modglin swam the backstroke with Van Mathias taking the breaststroke leg, while Gretchen Walsh swam butterfly, and Kate Douglass handled the freestyle. They finished in 3 minutes, 36.70 seconds.

The U.S. previously set the world record at the 2024 Paris Olympics with a time of 3:37.43. That relay team consisted of Ryan Murphy, Nicolas Fink, Walsh and Torri Huske.

Walsh and Douglass both already held world records going into the meet: Walsh in the 50-meter freestyle, 100-meter butterfly, the 4×100-meter medley relay and the mixed medley relay; Douglass in the 4×100-meter medley relay and mixed 4×100-meter freestyle relay. Both Douglass and Walsh train at University of Virginia and have five and four Olympic medals, respectively.

Modglin and Mathias are new to the record books, and neither was on the 2024 Olympic team. Mathias, a sprint specialist who had stopped competitive swimming for two years before returning to the sport in 2025, split a 57.30, nearly a full second faster than Fink’s split in Paris. Though he’s returned to the pool, he’s still working as the director of operations for University of Indiana’s swim team.

“Even just last week I was in the office pushing papers,” he said. “Now we’re in the pool breaking records. It’s really cool. I don’t take it for granted.”

Douglass also had a massive split, going 51.01 in the final 100. She said that, while waiting for the race, “we kind of threw out the idea of breaking a world record.”

“I could see during the race that we were slightly above world record pace,” she said. “I knew that I had a really fast split in me. … I was confident if I put up a good race we would break it.”

Walsh slightly improved her 100-meter butterfly split from Paris, going 54.99, down from 55.18. Murphy’s 2024 split (52.08) was 1.32 seconds faster than Modglin, a Team USA rookie at major international competitions.

“I’m still a little speechless,” the backstroker said after the race. “You watch Kate and Gretchen. They’ve been doing this for a while now. I think just being on a relay with them is such an honor.”

All four of the American swimmers also won medals earlier in the evening. Walsh flirted with the 50-meter butterfly world record and took gold, with Douglass finishing in silver position. Mathias earned silver in the 50-meter butterfly, and Modglin was second in the 100-meter backstroke.

The U.S. world record comes a year after it failed to qualify for the mixed medley finals at the 2025 World Championships.

Australia and Canada took silver and bronze in the Pan Pacs mixed medley relay, respectively. Taylor Ruck swam the freestyle leg for Canada and picked up her third bronze of the night, having previously finished third in the 50-meter butterfly and 100-meter backstroke. That was the biggest medal haul of anyone on Day 1.

Five Americans, four Australians and one Canadian won gold on the first day of Pan Pacs, the biggest meet of the year for swimming nations outside of Europe. That includes Katie Ledecky, the American star who continued her dominance in the 1,500-meter freestyle by holding off a strong effort from Australia’s Lani Pallister. Ledecky finished in 15:36.09, which she noted was slower than other times she’s had this season and more than nine seconds slower than her gold-winning time at 2025 Worlds.

Still, the nine-time Olympic gold medalist savored her first international medal won on home soil.

“I’m not going to take these opportunities for granted,” Ledecky said. “Even though I’m not super happy with the final time today, I still have a huge smile on my face.”

Earlier in the night, Pallister beat Canadian star Summer McIntosh for gold in the 200–meter freestyle.

“I really wanted to challenge myself with doing a double,” said Pallister, who has established herself as a major presence heading midway through the Olympic quad. “When you have an opportunity to race in (California) when the Olympics are here in two years and get up and race the best in the world with Summer and Katie and challenge yourself … then it’s an important opportunity to take.”

It was the second world record to fall Wednesday. In Paris at the European championships, the corresponding major event across the pond, Italy’s Sara Curtis, who also trains at the University of Virginia, broke the three-year-old 50-meter backstroke mark.
